submission.reasoning: On workstation5, user WORKSTATION5\wardog opened an interactive cmd.exe (proc-29da349e7e) with high integrity. From it, at 2020-10-23T06:36:43Z, they ran bitsadmin.exe (proc-826bdb1e01) with '/transfer /Download /priority Foreground'. The job pulled content from raw.githubusercontent.com (an Atomic Red Team T1197 resource) and saved it in the user's Temp folder under a .ps1 script name, bitsadmin1_flag.ps1. Using the BITS client to fetch a remote file into Temp as a PowerShell script matches ATT&CK T1197 (BITS Jobs), a living-off-the-land download technique. The atomic-red-team URL points to an attack emulation run, but the activity is the attack technique itself, so the verdict is malicious. No file entity for the downloaded script was found in the graph, so it is not listed as an artifact. Response: isolate the host, rotate the wardog credentials, and check for and remove the downloaded script and any BITS jobs that remain.
